declarations.name: AccessoryNotification.Attributes
declarations.comment:
These options represent attributes of this notification. This information can be used to decorate notifications to visually represent their types. It can also be use to group or display the notifications in a particular order.

These values should not be used to determine whether your notification should alert or not. Use AlertingContext for that information.

members.name: init
members.comment:
Creates a new option set from the given raw value.

This initializer always succeeds, even if the value passed as `rawValue`
exceeds the static properties declared as part of the option set. This
example creates an instance of `ShippingOptions` with a raw value beyond
the highest element, with a bit mask that effectively contains all the
declared static members.

    let extraOptions = ShippingOptions(rawValue: 255)
    print(extraOptions.isStrictSuperset(of: .all))
    // Prints "true"

- Parameter rawValue: The raw value of the option set to create. Each bit
  of `rawValue` potentially represents an element of the option set,
  though raw values may include bits that are not defined as distinct
  values of the `OptionSet` type.

members.name: rawValue

declarations.name: AccessoryNotification.Attributes.ArrayLiteralElement
declarations.comment: The type of the elements of an array literal.

declarations.name: AccessoryNotification.Attributes.Element
declarations.comment:
The element type of the option set.

To inherit all the default implementations from the `OptionSet` protocol,
the `Element` type must be `Self`, the default.

declarations.name: AccessoryNotification.Attributes.RawValue
declarations.comment:
The raw type that can be used to represent all values of the conforming
type.

Every distinct value of the conforming type has a corresponding unique
value of the `RawValue` type, but there may be values of the `RawValue`
type that don't have a corresponding value of the conforming type.

declarations.name: AccessoryNotification.DisplayDate
declarations.comment:
An enum representing the preferred date and format to be displayed with the notification.

- deliveryDate: display the notification's deliveryDate, typically displayed with minute accuracy
- contentDate: display a specific date that is different than the deliveryDate
    - an example: a calendar event with a timestamp in the future
    - typically displayed with minute accuracy
- allDayDate: display a specific date that is different than the deliveryDate
    - an example: an all day calendar event
    - should be displayed with day accuracy (ie Sunday or July 1st)
- hideDate: do not display a date with this notification

declarations.name: AccessoryNotification.File
declarations.comment:
A file resource associated with an accessory notification.

`File` represents media content that accompanies a notification, such as icons or attachments.

- Note: The underlying file data is managed by the system and provided only when requested
  in the context of an add or modify event.

members.name: url
members.signature: var url: URL { get async throws }
members.comment:
The URL of a file on the local device representing this `File`.

This URL is only accessible in the context of a notification addition or modification.
The file should be modified as needed and saved to your container within this interval.

members.name: type
members.comment:
The type of the file at `url`.

See [Supported File Types](https://developer.apple.com/documentation/usernotifications/unnotificationattachment#Supported-File-Types) for more information and a list of possible file types.

declarations.name: AccessoryNotification.Identifier
declarations.comment:
A notification is uniquely identified by a combination of the sourceIdentifier and notificationIdentifier.

- sourceIdentifier: a string identifier that represents the bundle that sent the notification.
- notificationIdentifier: a string identifier set by the sending bundle to uniquely identify this notification within the bundle namespace.

Both elements are required to uniquely identify a notification.

declarations.name: AlertingContext
declarations.comment: Provides hints to the accessory about the preferred alerting behavior for newly-added notifications.

members.name: shouldAlert
members.comment:
Convenience property to determine the preferred alerting behavior based on the notification state and Focus state of the device.

Accessories that do not wish to inspect individual properties on `AlertingContext` can use this property to get the preferred default alerting behavior.

members.comment: A flag to indicate whether a notification would be suppressed by a Focus mode on the phone.

members.name: notificationCanAlert
members.comment:
Flag to indicate whether a notification can alert.

A notification is considered to alert when it is presented onscreen and plays sounds and/or haptics.
Accessories should not alert if this flag is `false`. If this flag is `true`, an accessory may alert, but could also
choose not to based on other factors specfic to the accessory.

`notificationCanAlert` may be false for a newly-added notification if the notification has already alerted on another
device, or if the user has configured the notification to not alert.

> Note: This property is independent from whether a notification might be silenced due to the device being in a Focus mode.

members.name: removeNotifications
members.comment:
Remove notifications.

- Parameters:
 - identifiers: An array of notification identifiers to clear.
- Throws: An error if the system could not receive the request to remove notifications.

This method has equivalent behavior to clearing the same notifications from Notification Center on the phone. Actions are not sent to the app for removed notifications.
This method only throws for errors receiving the request to remove notifications. It does not throw if some of the identifiers could not be cleared because they have already been removed.
